local_checks.invariant: PR-triggered CI must not run contributor code with secrets, write tokens or publish/deploy authority
local_checks.result: Workflow triggers on pull_request (not pull_request_target) and push to main; top-level permissions contents: read; no secrets referenced (only literal test credentials for ephemeral service containers); no publish, deploy, registry push or cache-write-to-trusted-consumer step; upload-artifact only on failure with .auth excluded. Fork PR code runs with read-only token and no secrets, so no privileged boundary is crossed.

local_checks.invariant: Mutable build inputs must not let a lower-trust writer reach a trusted build output
local_checks.result: Actions are tag-pinned (actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-artifact@v4) not SHA-pinned, base images are tag-pinned (node:22.23-bookworm-slim, postgres:16-alpine, redis:8.8.2-alpine), MinIO/mc pinned to release tags. CI produces no released artifact and the Dockerfile image is built locally by the operator (docker compose build), not by CI, so no source-visible path from a mutable tag writer to a published/trusted artifact. Recorded as hardening only.

local_checks.invariant: Build context must not place secrets or developer artifacts into the runtime image
local_checks.result: .dockerignore excludes only node_modules, dist, .git (not .env). COPY backend/ and COPY frontend/ occur only in intermediate build stages; runtime stage copies only package*.json, dist, prisma, prisma.config.ts, src/generated, frontend/dist and data/avv, so a local backend/.env or root .env would not reach the shipped runtime image. Dockerfile uses npm install (not npm ci) with lockfiles copied; dependency resolution is lockfile-guided and no lower-trust writer is identified.

hardening_notes: docker-compose.yml publishes app 3000:3000 and minio 9000:9000 on all host interfaces while using NODE_ENV=development, JWT fallback local-dev-secret-change-me, default Nutzer change-me-now and MinIO root research/research-secret; bind to 127.0.0.1 ("127.0.0.1:3000:3000") so a dev stack on a LAN/VPS is not reachable with forgeable JWTs and known root credentials.
env.ts only rejects two literal placeholder JWT secrets in production; add a minimum length/entropy check (e.g. >= 32 bytes) so short non-placeholder secrets are rejected.
GitHub Actions are tag-pinned (@v4) rather than commit-SHA pinned; CI holds no secrets or write tokens so impact is limited, but SHA pinning closes the mutable-tag path if publishing is ever added.
Dockerfile uses `npm install` instead of `npm ci`; switch to `npm ci` so image builds fail rather than silently re-resolve when package.json and package-lock.json disagree.
.dockerignore does not exclude .env / **/.env; the runtime stage does not copy them, but excluding them keeps local secrets out of the build context and intermediate layers/build cache.
minio-init swallows `mc admin user add` failures with `|| true`; failures surface later at policy attach, but an explicit check would make secret-rotation failures clearer.

local_checks.invariant: Throttler tracker must identify the real client, and client-supplied X-Forwarded-For must not be trusted unless ingress strips it
local_checks.result: Global ThrottlerGuard (app.module.ts:47) uses @nestjs/throttler ^6.7 default tracker (req.ips[0] or req.ip). main.ts never calls app.set('trust proxy', ...), so req.ips is empty and req.ip is the TCP peer. X-Forwarded-For is therefore NOT trusted (no spoofing path), but every request arriving via Caddy is keyed on the Caddy container address.

local_checks.invariant: Per-client auth throttle (5/min) must not become a single global bucket that one anonymous client can exhaust for all users
local_checks.result: Prod compose publishes only Caddy (80/443); Caddyfile reverse_proxy app:3000 is the only path to the app, so all clients share one tracker value per handler. AUTH_THROTTLE 5/min on login, passwort-vergessen and passwort-setzen becomes a global per-route quota exhaustible by one anonymous client (candidate). Actual peer address seen by Node inside the Docker network is a deployment fact.

hardening_notes: Login and passwort-vergessen skip bcrypt for unknown emails (auth.service.ts:23, 34), which gives a timing signal for account existence. Compare against a dummy hash to equalize.
Logout (auth.controller.ts:60-64) only clears cookies. The JWT stays valid server-side until exp (default 8h) because there is no revocation list. Consider a per-user session epoch bumped on logout.

Login CSRF: POST /auth/login is public, and Nest's default urlencoded body parser accepts a cross-site top-level form POST. A victim could be logged into an attacker's Nutzer account. Impact is limited (all entries are readable by every Nutzer), but consider requiring a JSON content type or checking Origin on the public auth POSTs.

passwortSetzen is find-then-update (auth.service.ts:51-69), not atomic. Two concurrent submissions of the same token both succeed. Only the token holder benefits; consider updateMany with the token in the where clause.
The PasswortSetzenDto max length of 128 exceeds bcrypt's 72-byte truncation, so characters after byte 72 are silently ignored. LoginDto.passwort has no MaxLength (the Express body limit bounds it).
JwtStrategy skips the passwortGeaendertAm check when iat is absent (jwt.strategy.ts:59). This is reachable only with the signing secret; consider rejecting tokens without iat.
If trust proxy is later enabled as a fix, restrict it to the single Caddy hop (trust proxy 1). Otherwise a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For would let attackers rotate throttle keys.

local_checks.invariant: Recovery token is high-entropy, stored hashed, user-bound, expiring, single-use, and consumption invalidates sessions
local_checks.result: 32-byte randomBytes, SHA-256 stored in @unique column, lookup by hash, expiry checked (auth.service.ts:54), token and expiry nulled and passwortGeaendertAm set on use (59-68). Find-then-update is non-atomic, but concurrent reuse only benefits the same token holder. Link is a relative path, so no Host-header-derived URL. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: An anonymous reset request must not destroy another account's only working credential path
local_checks.result: Initial access and reset share one token slot (schema.prisma:37-39). Anonymous passwort-vergessen (auth.service.ts:38-45) overwrites the 7-day initial-access token that NutzerService issued (nutzer.service.ts:40-41). The replacement goes to ConsoleMailer (auth.module.ts:34), which only logs and never delivers (mailer.ts:13-17). No reissue endpoint exists, and email is unique, so the account cannot be recreated. Candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Login verifies the bcrypt hash for the looked-up user; the new password meets the policy
local_checks.result: bcrypt.compare against the DB hash. Pending users hold a random-UUID placeholder hash, so they cannot log in. The new password is limited to 12-128 chars plus a small denylist. The only enumeration signal is timing (bcrypt is skipped for unknown emails), which reveals account existence only. Holds; hardening noted.

local_checks.invariant: Client strips the recovery token from URL after reading
local_checks.result: Token read from queryParamMap then router.navigate with replaceUrl and empty queryParams. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: POST /api/v1/auth/logout must invalidate the issued access token server-side so that it is no longer accepted by JwtStrategy.validate
local_checks.result: Logout (auth.controller.ts:60-64) only calls res.clearCookie for accessToken/csrfToken. No denylist, token version, jti, or per-user session state exists; JwtStrategy.validate (jwt.strategy.ts:47-62) accepts any validly signed HS256 token with correct iss/aud whose sub exists and whose iat >= passwortGeaendertAm. Logout does not touch passwortGeaendertAm or any other field, so a token remains accepted until its exp (JWT_EXPIRES_IN default 8h, env.ts:61, auth.module.ts:22). Candidate raised.

local_checks.invariant: Client logout must reliably remove the ambient session credential from the device
local_checks.result: Frontend logout (auth.service.ts:49-55) clears local signals first and sends the logout POST fire-and-forget with errors swallowed; because accessToken is HttpOnly, the SPA cannot delete it itself. If the POST fails (offline PWA, network error), the cookie survives and the next app start calls GET /api/v1/auth/me (auth.service.ts:33), which re-establishes the previous Nutzer's session. The service worker caches only static assets (ngsw-config.json), so no API response copies persist. Folded into the same candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Password change/reset and account deletion revoke previously issued tokens
local_checks.result: passwortSetzen sets passwortGeaendertAm=new Date() (auth.service.ts:67) and validate rejects tokens with iat older than that (jwt.strategy.ts:59); deleted accounts are rejected by the DB existence lookup (jwt.strategy.ts:51-54). The iat-absent skip is owned by the peer JWT claim-binding unit. passwortVergessen only rotates the reset token and does not change the password or sessions, which is correct.

local_checks.invariant: Account offboarding (disable/delete) revokes access
local_checks.result: No disable/deactivate flag and no Nutzer delete path exist in the source (NutzerService only has create/findEigeneDaten/updateEigeneDaten). The only revocation levers are an operator-side DB row delete, which the existence check honours, or a password reset. So no source path grants stale authorization after offboarding. The missing disable flag is noted as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Session fixation: login issues a fresh credential that is not attacker-preset
local_checks.result: Login always signs a new JWT (auth.service.ts:27) and sets fresh accessToken and CSRF cookies (auth.controller.ts:26-41). No server-side session identifier can be fixed. No issue.

critic_reason: critic-w1: no unit covered logout/offboarding session revocation
hardening_notes: No account disable/deactivate flag exists; offboarding a Nutzer currently requires deleting the DB row (which the JwtStrategy existence check honours) or forcing a password reset. Consider an aktiv flag checked in JwtStrategy.validate.

JwtStrategy.validate skips the passwortGeaendertAm comparison when iat is absent (jwt.strategy.ts:59); tokens signed by this backend always carry iat, and this is owned by the peer JWT claim-binding unit.
loescheAuthCookies calls clearCookie without the secure/sameSite attributes used when setting; this works in current browsers but mirroring the set options is more robust.

local_checks.invariant: Every cookie-authenticated non-safe method requires a matching non-empty csrfToken cookie and X-CSRF-Token header
local_checks.result: JwtAuthGuard runs csrfIstGueltig after passport auth. Non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests need a string, non-empty, strictly equal cookie and header. Array or duplicate headers fail the typeof check. The token is 32 random bytes minted at login.

local_checks.invariant: Inventory: no authenticated mutation bypasses JwtAuthGuard, and no CORS or method-override makes a custom header forgeable cross-site
local_checks.result: All authenticated mutations are covered by a class-level @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard): POST/PATCH /nutzer, POST/PATCH/DELETE /wareneintraege. No controller uses the bare AuthGuard('jwt'). There is no enableCors and no method-override middleware, so a cross-site custom header triggers a preflight that fails. The accessToken cookie is also SameSite=Strict. The unauthenticated POSTs (login, logout, passwort-*) carry no ambient credential for a state change on the victim. Login/logout CSRF is noted under hardening.

local_checks.result: istEigeneApi checks the origin and the /api/ prefix before the header is attached. Holds.

local_checks.invariant: Every /api/v1/nutzer route requires an authenticated Nutzer and binds identity from the verified JWT (request.user.id), never from request input.
local_checks.result: Class-level @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) at nutzer.controller.ts:9 covers POST /, GET /me, PATCH /me. All three pass request.user.id (set by JwtStrategy.validate from DB lookup of payload.sub) to the service; there is no :id route parameter, so no other Nutzer's record is addressable.

local_checks.invariant: Body fields cannot override protected Nutzer state (email, passwortHash, passwortGeaendertAm, mussPasswortSetzen, passwortSetzenToken, erstelltVonId, id) on create or self-update.
local_checks.result: Global ValidationPipe uses whitelist+forbidNonWhitelisted (main.ts:15), DTOs expose only vorname/nachname/(email on create)/standortId, and the service builds Prisma data from explicit fields only (nutzer.service.ts:21-35, 60-64). updateEigeneDaten uses where:{id} from the JWT and cannot change email or credentials. createNutzer sets erstelltVonId from the JWT, mussPasswortSetzen=true, a random bcrypt placeholder and a hashed 32-byte token. Email is @unique so creating an account cannot overwrite or take over an existing account.

local_checks.invariant: Account provisioning authority and self-assigned Standort match the documented policy.
local_checks.result: CONTEXT.md (Nutzer glossary entry) states that every Nutzer may create new Nutzer accounts, no self-signup, no roles; architecture summary records self-editable name/Standort as design. Returning the raw setup link to the creator is documented design (nutzer.service.ts:17-19). Creating an account for a new email and holding its setup link does not grant access to any pre-existing account. No weaker alternate path to the same state change exists (auth.controller only offers login/logout/password flows keyed on email/token). No violation of the stated policy.

hardening_notes: backend/src/wareneintrag/wareneintrag.service.ts:162-165,182: pruefeBesitz is find-then-act; binding ownership in the write itself (e.g. updateMany/deleteMany with where {id, erfasstVonId: nutzerId} and checking count) would keep the owner-only invariant atomic if ownership ever becomes mutable.

backend/prisma/schema.prisma:23: Nutzer.email is @unique but case-sensitive and not normalized in CreateNutzerDto/login, so a Nutzer can create a case-variant lookalike account (e.g. Victim@firma vs victim@firma); normalizing email to lowercase on create/login/passwort-vergessen avoids confusing duplicate identities. No existing account is taken over.

backend/src/wareneintrag/wareneintrag.service.ts:185-191: pruefeBesitz uses findUniqueOrThrow on an unvalidated :id param; a ParseUUIDPipe on the route would return 400/404 instead of a Prisma error (500) for malformed or unknown ids.

local_checks.invariant: Full-text search raw SQL binds every caller-controlled value as a parameter, never as SQL text
local_checks.result: sucheMitVolltext uses the Prisma.$queryRaw tagged template (service.ts:96-120); suche, praefixSuche, proSeite and the offset are interpolated as bind parameters. The optional avvCodeId/standortId filters are Prisma.sql tagged fragments (91-94) that are also parameterized; the only non-parameter composition is Prisma.empty. No $queryRawUnsafe/$executeRawUnsafe or Prisma.raw is used anywhere in the unit.

local_checks.invariant: The to_tsquery input built from user text cannot inject tsquery operators or cause a syntax error
local_checks.result: praefixSuche is made only from /[\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu matches, each followed by ':*' and joined with ' & ' (service.ts:95). No ASCII tsquery operators (&|!()<>:') can reach it. An input with no words gives '' (to_tsquery returns an empty query with a NOTICE, not an error). websearch_to_tsquery never raises an error on syntax. Neither form can inject.

local_checks.invariant: Query parameters used in Prisma where-objects cannot become operator objects (Prisma operator injection)
local_checks.result: main.ts does not override the Express 5 'simple' query parser (querystring), so query values are only strings or string arrays and never nested objects. listeAlle (service.ts:60-63) and the AVV search (avv.controller.ts:17-28) therefore cannot receive {not:..}/{contains:..} operator objects. A repeated key gives an array, and that only causes a Prisma or TypeError 500. All authenticated Nutzer may read every entry by design (CONTEXT.md), so filter manipulation would not widen access anyway.

local_checks.invariant: Indirect/second-order injection: stored freitext or object keys are not reused in a dangerous sink
local_checks.result: Stored freitext only returns as JSON data. Object keys stored in the foto_*_url columns are always server-generated 'wareneintraege/<randomUUID>' (object-storage.service.ts:42) and are only passed to the S3 SDK GetObject/DeleteObject as a Key. No stored value is concatenated into SQL, shell, path or template.

hardening_notes: wareneintrag.controller.ts findAll: query params avvCodeId/standortId/suche are not validated (no DTO with @IsUUID/@IsString/@MaxLength). Repeated keys produce arrays that cause a TypeError at service.ts:95 or Prisma/Postgres type errors (HTTP 500). Add a query DTO so these return 400 and the length of suche is capped.

suche has no explicit length cap. Up to about 8k ':*' prefix terms (bounded only by Node's 16 KiB header limit) are ANDed in to_tsquery against the GIN index. The cost is bounded and throttled, but capping suche length and the number of terms would make DB work predictable.

seite is accepted up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so seite*proSeite can exceed 2^53 and give imprecise or invalid OFFSET/skip values (500). Cap seite at a realistic maximum, or bound it by ceil(gesamt/proSeite).

wareneintrag.service.ts update: ersetzeFoto runs concurrently via Promise.all and deletes old objects before the DB update commits. A failed sibling upload or a failed DB update leaves DB rows pointing at deleted keys, and concurrent PATCHes orphan newly uploaded objects. This is an integrity and storage-hygiene issue on one's own entry only; delete old keys after the DB update succeeds.
Add limits.files: 3 and limits.parts to FOTO_UPLOAD_OPTIONS as defense in depth, in addition to the maxCount per field.

local_checks.result: Every present file is validated by FileTypeValidator with a strict jpeg|png|webp regex and fallbackToMimetype:false (controller.ts:34,54-64,70-78), plus a 10 MB MaxFileSizeValidator. local_checks.invariant: Presigned references are bound to operation, exact key and short expiry, and do not outlive deletion
local_checks.result: getSignedUrl signs a GetObjectCommand for one exact bucket/key with expiresIn 900 s (object-storage.service.ts:10,60-63). local_checks.invariant: Upload processing (multer buffering) happens only after authentication and CSRF
local_checks.result: The controller has @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) (controller.ts:82). Nest runs guards (the global ThrottlerGuard, then the JWT and CSRF check in jwt-auth.guard.ts:8-23) before the FileFieldsInterceptor, so an anonymous client cannot make the server buffer multipart content.

local_checks.invariant: Multipart parsing has aggregate bounds on non-file fields (count, size, parts), not only a per-file size
local_checks.result: FOTO_UPLOAD_OPTIONS only sets limits.fileSize (controller.ts:38). No fields, fieldSize, parts or files limit is set. Caddyfile reverse_proxy sets no request_body max_size, and the prod compose sets no memory limit on app. Candidate h3-input:wareneintrag-multipart-unbounded-fields.

local_checks.invariant: Persisted per-entry free text has a maximum length so shared list responses stay bounded
local_checks.result: The freitext DTOs have only @IsString @MinLength(1) and no @MaxLength (dto lines 7-9). Through multipart the value can reach the busboy 1 MiB fieldSize default. The column is TEXT, and the generated tsvector stays small for repetitive text. Every GET list (default 20, max 100 per page, controller.ts:28-29,94-95) returns the full freitext of the newest entries to all Nutzer. Candidate h3-input:wareneintrag-freitext-unbounded-length.

local_checks.invariant: Pagination parameters are bounded integers
local_checks.result: parseGanzeZahl requires an integer, proSeite in 1..100 and seite in 0..MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (controller.ts:94-112). LIMIT/take is bounded at 100. A very large seite gives a very large OFFSET, which at worst makes a table-bounded scan or a 500 when seite*proSeite leaves the safe integer range. This is not amplification beyond the table size.

local_checks.invariant: Search input size and resulting DB work are bounded
local_checks.result: No explicit length cap on suche. It is bounded by Node's 16 KiB header limit to about 8k prefix terms against a GIN index, and requests are throttled at 60/min per tracker (app.module.ts:31). The AVV search is ILIKE over 834 rows with take 50. I found no superlinear or persistent shared effect, so I recorded this as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted query shapes do not reach a process-fatal error

Array avvCodeId/standortId values cause Prisma or Postgres errors. All of these are caught by Nest's exception layer and return 500. The process does not exit.

local_checks.invariant: Server- or other-user-controlled data (freitext, Nutzer names, Standort names, AVV bezeichnung, email, error messages, presigned photo URLs) never reaches an HTML/script/URL execution sink without Angular escaping or sanitization.
local_checks.result: Repo-wide grep over frontend/src finds no innerHTML/outerHTML, document.write, bypassSecurityTrust*, DomSanitizer, eval/new Function, [href] or [attr.href] bindings, window.open, postMessage listeners. All untrusted text is rendered via {{ }} interpolation or [value]/[title]/[alt] property bindings (escaped). Photo URLs bind to (URL context sanitized by Angular; img src is not script-executing). The raw setup link is bound only to input [value] and cdkCopyToClipboard, not to an anchor. No DOM-XSS source-to-sink path exists.

local_checks.invariant: No URL/query-controlled value drives navigation or redirect to an attacker-chosen destination (open redirect, javascript:/data: navigation).
local_checks.result: All navigateByUrl/createUrlTree targets are hard-coded literals ('/', '/login', '/login?passwortGesetzt=1', '/wareneintraege'). No returnUrl/redirect parameter is read. passwort-setzen reads ?token only into a private field sent as JSON body to the same-origin API, then strips it from the URL via replaceUrl; login only checks presence of passwortGesetzt to show a fixed snackbar string. No navigation confusion.

local_checks.invariant: Service worker and browser storage do not persist personalized/authenticated responses that could be served to a later account or after logout.
local_checks.result: ngsw-config.json defines only assetGroups (index.html, *.js, *.css, favicon, manifest, and same-origin image/font extensions); there are no dataGroups, so /api/* responses are not cached by the SW. API paths do not end in the cached image/font extensions, and photos are served from FILES_DOMAIN (a different origin, outside SW asset matching). Auth state is held only in in-memory signals derived from /api/v1/auth/me with the token in an HttpOnly cookie; the only localStorage key is 'farbmodus' with values whitelisted to 'hell'|'dunkel'. No cross-account or post-logout cache path.

local_checks.invariant: State-changing SPA pages cannot be framed cross-origin and CSP limits script execution to same-origin bundles.
local_checks.result: helmet is applied globally via app.use in main.ts before listen (ServeStaticModule-served SPA included by source ordering) with CSP default-src 'self', script-src 'self' (no unsafe-inline/eval), object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', frame-ancestors 'self'; helmet defaults also emit X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN; Referrer-Policy no-referrer protects the setup/reset token during the brief window before URL stripping. Cross-origin clickjacking of state-changing actions is prevented by source-visible headers (deployed header passthrough via Caddy reverse_proxy is default-preserving).

local_checks.invariant: Client code does not leak the CSRF token or session handling to foreign origins.
local_checks.result: istEigeneApi requires a '/api/' relative prefix or an absolute URL whose origin equals window.location.origin with /api/ pathname; the X-CSRF-Token header is attached only then. Note that '/api/...' prefix check also accepts only path-relative URLs (a protocol-relative '//host/api' does not start with '/api/'). No leak path.

hardening_notes: CSP style-src includes 'unsafe-inline' (backend/src/security-headers.ts); no script injection sink exists, so this only widens CSS-injection impact if a future HTML sink is introduced.
frame-ancestors 'self' permits same-origin framing; 'none' would be stricter since the SPA does not frame itself.

No Cache-Control: no-store is set on authenticated /api/v1 JSON responses (no match for Cache-Control in backend/src); browser HTTP cache could retain entry lists after logout on a shared device. Not a SW issue; consider no-store on API responses.

The password-setup/reset token is present in the initial URL (history entry replaced after component construction); Referrer-Policy no-referrer and replaceUrl mitigate, but the token is also visible to the raw setup link shown in nutzer-anlegen (by design).

local_checks.result: accessToken is httpOnly, sameSite strict, secure when NODE_ENV=production and path /. csrfToken is deliberately non-HttpOnly for the double-submit pattern. The Dockerfile and prod compose set NODE_ENV=production. Dev compose sets development on HTTP localhost.

local_checks.result: The prod compose passes INITIAL_NUTZER_PASSWORT and JWT_SECRET from the server .env with no defaults. required() throws on empty values. local_checks.invariant: No open redirects; TLS is enforced at ingress; no security TODOs or token logging; dependency advisories are tracked
local_checks.result: All navigateByUrl targets are constant strings, so there are no redirect/next/url parameters. Caddy site blocks use automatic HTTPS. ConsoleMailer logs only the recipient, never the raw token. There are no security TODO/FIXME/HACK comments. The accepted Prisma transitive advisories are documented. Lockfiles exist, but the Dockerfile uses npm install rather than npm ci (supply chain is peer-owned).

hardening_notes: Logout only clears cookies; the HS256 JWT stays valid until expiry (8h default) with no server-side revocation, so a copied token survives logout.

WareneintragService.ersetzeFoto (wareneintrag.service.ts:308-313) deletes the old object before the DB update commits, so a failed update (e.g. an invalid avvCodeId FK) leaves the owner's entry referencing a deleted key. Delete old objects only after the DB update succeeds.

The dev docker-compose.yml publishes MinIO 9000 and app 3000 on all interfaces with hardcoded MinIO root credentials (research/research-secret) and a default JWT secret. These are safe only on a developer workstation; binding to 127.0.0.1 would prevent accidental LAN exposure.
passwortVergessen performs an extra DB write for existing accounts only, which is a small timing difference relative to the comment's claim of non-disclosure (peer recovery unit owns enumeration).
Email lookup is case-sensitive (findUnique on the raw string), so 'Max@x' and 'max@x' can exist as separate Nutzer accounts.

local_checks.invariant: An anonymous caller cannot invalidate or replace the 7-day Initial-Zugang token that a Nutzer issued for a new account, and there is a path to recover or reissue it
local_checks.result: The invariant is violated. Anonymous POST /auth/passwort-vergessen overwrites the single shared passwortSetzenToken/Ablauf columns of any existing Nutzer, including a mussPasswortSetzen=true account. The replacement token goes only to ConsoleMailer, which does not deliver it. No endpoint reissues the setup link, and email is @unique, so the account cannot be recreated either. Recorded as candidate backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:passwortVergessen:overwrites-initial-zugang-token.

local_checks.invariant: Password-set tokens are single use and time bound
local_checks.result: The token is 32 random bytes and stored as a SHA-256 hash with @unique. Expiry is checked with a strict < comparison against now. Success nulls the token and sets passwortGeaendertAm. The find-then-update is not atomic, so two concurrent submissions with the same valid token could both succeed. Both come from the token holder, so there is no cross-principal gain (race detail belongs to the peer recovery unit).

local_checks.invariant: Standort attribution and the edit state transitions of an entry cannot be forged by another principal
local_checks.result: create() takes standortId from the DB copy of the caller's current Nutzer.standortId, not from client input. A Nutzer can self-assign any Standort via PATCH /nutzer/me, which CONTEXT.md and the architecture document as intended. update() and remove() check ownership before acting. ersetzeFoto deletes the old object before the DB update. If the DB update fails (for example on an invalid avvCodeId FK), the owner's own entry points at a deleted key. That affects only the same principal (hardening).
